body:
**The 2018–2020 drawdown, contemporaneous reporting**
- Investor wealth fell about 44% in FY19 (43.7% through Dec 2018). Monthly falls were 11.9% in May, 12.3% in June and 20% in September 2018, per SEBI data — [IANS/Hans India, 13 Jan 2019](https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/Latest-News/2019-01-13/Made-a-mistake-says-Porinju-Veliyath-after-investor-wealth-eroded-by-44/474694). This conflicts with the firm's later FY19 figure of -31.87%. The gap is probably the measurement window (FY to date in Dec vs full FY), but it is not reconciled.
- **LEEL Electricals (ex-Lloyd Electric):** Equity Intelligence held about 5.4% by Oct 2017 and about 8% by Feb 2018. LEEL fell from ₹215 to ₹127 in five days, and was about 80% below cost in most accounts. Veliyath alleged that about ₹340 crore of the ₹1,550 crore Havells sale proceeds was diverted to promoter entities (including Fedders Electric) and filed a SEBI complaint seeking a forensic audit. These are his allegations, not a regulatory finding. His letter said: "in hindsight it looks a mistake", and that his assumption that siphoning was hard under the new regime "appears faulty" — [Hans India](https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/Latest-News/2019-01-13/Made-a-mistake-says-Porinju-Veliyath-after-investor-wealth-eroded-by-44/474694). LEEL in turn accused him of deliberately deflating its stock. That is a company allegation, unverified — [blog summary](https://rakesh-jhunjhunwala.in/my-strategy-of-betting-big-on-chor-companies-has-backfired-porinju-veliyath/)
- **"Chor" stocks:** In 2015–2018 he publicly advocated low-priced, poor-governance "chor" companies for their re-rating potential. He later said the strategy "backfired" and vowed to invest only in companies with integrity, while also claiming the advice was "misunderstood" — [blog compilations of ET interviews](https://rakesh-jhunjhunwala.in/i-burnt-fingers-badly-with-chor-stocks-porinju-veliyath-concedes-defeat-vows-to-stay-away-from-chors-invest-only-in-cos-with-integrity/); [also](https://rakesh-jhunjhunwala.in/my-advice-reg-chor-stocks-was-misunderstood-by-investors-says-porinju-veliyath-while-issuing-buy-call/)
- A ValuePickr user estimated a 55.7% erosion from Jan 2018 to Aug 2019 for a fully invested client. A blog commenter reported -42% vs -28% for the Nifty Smallcap 100 to 12 Aug 2019. Both are anecdotal — [ValuePickr](https://forum.valuepickr.com/t/pms-funds-india/10842?page=14); [blog](https://indianhiddengem.blogspot.com/2017/04/equity-intelligence-pms-review.html)
- He publicly called the mid/small-cap sell-off "overdone" in July 2018 ("Paranoia will vanish soon"); the PMS then lost about 51% more in FY20 — [Porinju on X, Jul 2018](https://twitter.com/porinju/status/1019917694076768256?lang=en). In a mid-2019 investor letter he blamed the Budget and an 18-month small-cap bear market — [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.in/india-market-news-porinju-veliyath-blames-the-budget-for-bear-market-in-smaller-stocks/articleshow/70277012.cms). Subscribers reportedly redeemed in waves after 2018 — [VRD Nation](https://www.vrdnation.com/famous-investors-porinju-veliyath-value-investor-equity-intelligence/)
- He later conceded that 2018 and 2019 were "very challenging" — [Money9](https://www.money9.com/news/markets/market-news/porinju-veliyath-who-delivered-153-return-to-investors-in-fy21-tells-where-to-invest-now-47322)

| Quarter (standalone) | Materials ÷ revenue | OPM `[SCR]` | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| FY25 | 63.8% | 20% | |
| FY26 | 63.2% | 21% | |
| Q2 FY26 | 63.5% | 22% | |
| Q1 FY27 | 66.5% | 18% | "Steel, pig iron, aluminium, copper significant increases"; "we have taken one [price increase]" `[CC-Q1FY27]` |
| **Q2 FY27** | **67.9%** | **15%** | +440 bps YoY. "Most of it is inflationary… relatively small portion… mix" `[CC-Q2FY27]` |
Method: (materials consumed + traded − change in inventories) ÷ (sales + other operating income) `[Q2R]`.

- **Why the lag is structural, in three mechanisms.**
  1. **Purchases from sister companies are cost-plus,** so their cost inflation passes *into* CIL almost at once.
  2. **Sales are on order books at contracted prices** (DC projects, rail/defence tenders "at agreed prices… price change mechanisms few and far between" `[CC-Q2FY27]`), so inflation passes *out* with a lag. **The minority-owned listed entity carries the timing mismatch.**
  3. **Inventory rose to ₹1,355 cr (Sep-26) from ₹1,168 cr (Mar-26)** `[Q2R]`, bought at higher costs, so Q3 COGS still carries the inflated cost layer.
- **Sensitivity** [EST]. If metal-linked content is ~35–50% of material cost (castings, forgings, sheet, Al; unverified, ask a supplier), a 10% rise in the metal basket costs **~220–320 bps of sales** before pricing. The observed −440 bps fits ~12–15% basket inflation plus some mix and freight. Analyst: "pig iron… up 14–20% YoY" `[CC-Q1FY27]`.
- **Leading indicators (all public, dated):** BigMint/SteelOrbis/Mysteel India pig iron and long-steel weekly prices; LME Al/Cu. Late-Oct/Nov-2026 readings show pig iron **flat to softer** (NMDC auction −₹300/t; SteelOrbis ₹16,500/t ex-works "stable") and the long-steel index down three weeks running `[WEB: SteelOrbis, Mysteel, single-source each]`. **This is the cost side turning before the P&L shows it.**
- **Pass-through history** [EST, from the `[SCR]` annual OPM]: in FY21–22 commodities rose and OPM sat at 14%; it recovered to 16% in FY23. That suggests a **2–4 quarter lag** for full pass-through in the last cycle, helped then by CPCB IV+ pricing, which is not available this time.

body:
1. **Margin bands are reliable, growth-shape talk is not.** Every company met its FY26 margin guidance: Persistent +90 bp vs ~+100 bp, Coforge 14.4% vs 14%, Mphasis 15.3% in its band, KPIT 20.8% vs 21%. Statements about *when* growth comes back ("robust H2", "meaningful Q4", vertical recoveries) met about two-thirds of the time. **Base case for an IT "growth returns next quarter / in H2" statement: about a coin-flip-plus. For a margin band: near-certain unless revenue falls.**
2. **The New Labour Code one-time charge (Q3FY26)** hit Persistent (230 bp) and Mphasis (INR 355 mn exceptional). Score on the adjusted basis (clarification C).
3. **Wage hikes in Q2/Q3** cost 150–180 bp every year at every company. They are always guided and always roughly as guided.
4. **Company EBIT/EBITDA ≠ screener.** Screener-derived (OP − depreciation)/sales is within 0.1 pp of company EBIT only for Mphasis. Persistent FY26 is 16.2% vs 15.6%, and Q2FY27 is 10.0% vs 15.0% because of Nagarro transaction costs. Coforge FY26 is 13.7% vs 14.4% (hedge reclassification). KPIT EBITDA is 20.8% vs 18.9% OPM. **IT margin calls must be resolved on the company figure (assisted), not the structured screener path.** This is the reason the new `ebit_margin_pct` measure takes a CSV override.
5. **Acquisitions blur growth promises.** Encora (Coforge, from May-26), Nagarro (Persistent, ~Dec-26/Jan-27), TAP/Red Oak (Mphasis) and Caresoft (KPIT) all inflate reported growth. Promises made before a deal have to be scored on an organic basis, or voided.
